Statement 2.text: The venue must have comprehensive step-free access throughout, accommodating wheelchair users fully

Statement 3.text: The format should avoid prolonged standing, with seating available throughout

Statement 4.text: The venue should be in central London, within easy distance of Waterloo, in Zone 1 or Zone 2

Statement 5.text: The company should cover the full cost of the evening including food and drinks

Statement 6.text: The venue should be quiet enough for conversation without needing to raise voices

Statement 7.text: A private or semi-private space should be used to aid conversation and hearing

Statement 8.text: The atmosphere should feel relaxed and celebratory, not formal or work-like

Statement 9.text: The venue should have energy and atmosphere

Statement 10.text: Good quality food is a priority, with vegetarian options available

Statement 11.text: Adequate non-alcoholic drink options must be available

Statement 12.text: A set menu format can work well for group dining

Statement 13.text: There should be a structured activity at the start of the event to facilitate cross-team mixing and reduce departmental clustering

Statement 14.text: There should be no structured activity; a good restaurant with relaxed dining is sufficient

Statement 15.text: Any activity should feel fun and voluntary rather than forced or contrived

Statement 16.text: Hands-on activities (e.g. escape rooms, cooking classes, cocktail making) work better than passive ones for bonding

Statement 17.text: The second half of the event should be relaxed and unstructured

Statement 18.text: The event must actively facilitate genuine connection between engineering and marketing teams, not just co-existence in the same room

Statement 19.text: Attendees should be free to choose who they talk to during unstructured time

Statement 20.text: The event should give people something to talk about or do together

Statement 21.text: The venue has some outdoor space
